symptom: The shared untrusted claimed-instant validator admitted a syntactically valid timestamp with a 1,000,000-digit fractional second; its chronology comparator pads fractions to the larger input length. The corresponding authority-metadata schema also admitted arbitrary fractional length. This creates an avoidable unbounded string-processing and allocation surface for caller-provided metadata; no external exploitation, N2 execution, scoring or production impact was observed.
lesson: Arbitrary fractional precision is not required to preserve nanosecond ordering and permits unbounded caller-controlled timestamp length. Bound input length before regex and Date.parse, align the schema's lexical fractional limit, and retain high-precision synthetic chronology coverage.
guardrail: Reject claimed timestamps longer than 90 characters and fractional seconds longer than 64 ASCII digits in the shared untrusted helper; mirror the 64-digit limit and maxLength 90 in the authority-metadata schema. Verify 64-digit acceptance, 65-digit rejection, long-input rejection, manifest digest parity and submillisecond comparison. These are structural resource bounds only, never trusted time or scoring authority.
